question_text: Find the set E of x for which the binomial expansion of (3 − 4x)^(3/4) is valid.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the set — how you take 3 out of the bracket, and the condition on x that makes the expansion valid.
insider_note: A fractional index expands only in the form (1 + y) with |y| < 1, so factor the 3 out first. The answer is an open interval — the end points are excluded.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take out the 3
steps.margin_note: First mark. A binomial with a fractional index expands only in the form (1 + y) with |y| < 1, so factor 3 out of the bracket.

recall.must_convey: That (3 − 4x) to the power 3/4 is 3 to the power 3/4 times (1 − 4x/3) to the power 3/4, valid when |4x/3| < 1.
accept: take three out to get three to the three by four times one minus four x by three to the three by four, valid when mod four x by three is less than one
factor out the three so the bracket is one minus something
the expansion is valid when the modulus of four x by three is less than one
three bayataki teeste one minus four x by three, mod four x by three less than one
write it as a power of one minus four x by three

steps.why: The expansion of (1 + y)ᵖ for a fractional p is an infinite series that converges only for |y| < 1; the leading constant must be pulled out first.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 3 to the power 3/4 outside.

steps.label: Solve for x
steps.margin_note: Second mark. |4x/3| < 1 gives |x| < 3/4, an open interval.

recall.must_convey: That |4x/3| < 1 gives |x| < 3/4, so E is the open interval (−3/4, 3/4).

x lies between minus three by four and three by four
the set is the open interval minus three quarters to three quarters

steps.why: The end points are excluded because at |y| = 1 the series does not converge for this index.
